report: Abstract: This review concerns the 77-page version arXiv:2212.13746v2 by Seonwoo Kim and Insuk Seo. Two Major findings concern the additional models in Section 5: the stated pairwise hitting times and limiting rates are mutually inconsistent, and the printed directed-Ising rates do not preserve the asserted Gibbs measure. Several local domain, normalization and proof corrections are also established. The arguments below distinguish these findings from a disproof of the principal Metropolis–Hastings or purely cyclic metastability results. Scientific adjudication and independent acceptance remain pending.
Author: Math2025 scientific review
Date: 29 October 2026

Title: Initial scientific review of
Approximation method to metastability
# Identity, version and scope

The assigned paper is Approximation method to metastability: an application to non-reversible, two-dimensional Ising and Potts models without external fields, by Seonwoo Kim and Insuk Seo, M25-0498. The journal record is Annals of Probability 53(2) (2025), 597–667, DOI https://doi.org/10.1214/24-AOP1717. The actual reviewed file is arXiv:2212.13746v2, dated 4 January 2023, with 77 PDF pages. All page and equation locators below refer to this file [KS], whose printed and PDF page numbers agree.

All text in Sections 1–9 and Appendices A–D was read, including the references. The eight figures and the source pages used for the findings were inspected as rendered images. The cited Godrèche–Bray paper [GB] was acquired separately; its selected pages 1, 7–13 and 19 were read and visually inspected. This is a dependency check, not an additional assigned-paper review.

The current official arXiv record still lists v2. The consulted author publication pages did not identify a correction to this item [Metadata]. This is a bounded observation, not proof that no correction exists. An actual request for the individual publisher PDF returned HTML rather than a PDF; its response was preserved. The 71-page journal article was therefore not compared. Findings are not automatically attributed to its final text. No missing program or unavailable publisher file is treated as a mathematical defect.
# Framework and operative assumptions

Equation reference: eq:H. The state space is \(S^\Lambda\), with \(\Lambda=\mathbb T_K\times\mathbb T_L\), \(11\leq K\leq L\), \(S=\{1,\ldots,q\}\), and \(q\geq2\). The limit \(\beta\to\infty\) is taken at fixed \(K,L,q\). The Hamiltonian and Gibbs probability are \[
 H(\sigma)=\sum_{\{x,y\}:x\sim y}{\bf1}_{\{\sigma(x)\ne\sigma(y)\}},
 \qquad \mu_\beta(\sigma)=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H(\sigma)}.\] Each unordered nearest-neighbor edge is counted once. Bold spins denote monochromatic ground states. These conventions, periodic boundaries, and the positivity of the rates are retained in every example below.

For MH dynamics the edge height is the larger endpoint energy. For the cyclic dynamics, \(q\geq3\), only the forward rotation \(\tau_x\) is permitted, and the edge height is the maximum energy over the entire local spin orbit. Thus the conductance identity (3.3) uses different heights for the two chains. The respective barriers are \(2K+2\) and \(2K+4\). The principal prefactor is \(\kappa=b+2e\), where \(b>0\) is the bulk constant and \(e>0\) the edge constant. Nonempty disjoint ground-state sets are required for the potential-theoretic statements.
# Substantive findings

Problem 1 (P1: incompatible hitting times and limiting rates).  Severity: Major, localized to Theorem 5.2. Theorem 5.2(2)–(3), pages 18–19, equations (5.2)–(5.3), assigns both the limiting mean hitting time \(\kappa_{|b-a|}\) and the limiting jump rate \(\kappa_{|b-a|}^{-1}\). Together with its stated prefactor asymptotics these assertions cannot all hold.
## Decisive calculation

Equation reference: eq:uv, eq:four. Choose the permitted parameters \(q=4\), \(p=1/2\) and \(L=K+1\). Write \[u=\kappa_1=\kappa_3,\qquad v=\kappa_2.\] Since \(\widehat p=1\) and \(\nu_0=1\), equation (5.3) gives \[
 u\longrightarrow \frac38,\qquad v\longrightarrow\frac12
 \quad(K\to\infty).\] The chain specified in part (3) has rate \(a=1/u\) to either neighboring spin on the four-cycle and rate \(b_0=1/v\) to the opposite spin. Label its states \(0,1,2,3\) for this calculation only. With target 0, symmetry gives mean hitting times \(x\) from 1 or 3 and \(y\) from 2. The exact backward equations are \[2ax-ay=1,\qquad -2ax+(2a+b_0)y=1.\] Their solution is \[
 x=\frac{u(u+3v)}{2(u+v)},\qquad
 y=\frac{2uv}{u+v},\qquad
 x-u=\frac{u(v-u)}{2(u+v)}.\] This was also checked by independently forming the full \(4\times4\) generator and solving its killed \(3\times3\) system exactly.
## Counterevidence, dependency and repair

Equal off-diagonal rates do give the advertised mean \(u\). Thus the principal purely cyclic case and the equal-rate cases are not counterexamples to themselves. The problem arises from using unequal pair-specific quantities simultaneously as inverse rates and target hitting times. The all-other-states exit-time formula, by itself, is consistent with the total jump rate.

This disproves the joint assertion of the additional-model theorem, but does not determine which of its rates, hitting-time formula, or prefactor formula is the correct one. Repair requires deriving a consistent effective generator and solving \(-Qg=1\) on the complement of the target. Alternatively, if the pairwise hitting constants are retained, the generator must be derived separately. The comparison in Remark 5.3 needs reassessment accordingly. The \(p=1\) principal cyclic results and the MH results are not refuted by this calculation.

Problem 2 (P2: the printed directed rates fail Gibbs stationarity).  Severity: Major, localized to Section 5.2. Pages 19–20 define one exponential of a weighted directional energy increment and assert that \(\mu_\beta\) is invariant for every \(p\in[0,1]\). That assertion is false for the displayed generator and Hamiltonian.
## Exact admissible counterexample
## Alternative readings and the cited reference

The source rates contain no positive part and no sum of exponentials; both details were checked in the page image. Changing the temperature convention or multiplying all rates by a common positive factor cannot make the nonzero balance residual vanish.

The cited reference [19], Godrèche–Bray [GB], Section 3.3, equations (3.13)–(3.14), pages 10–11, treats the purely NE directed rate and a three-neighbor extension. Its exponential interpolation (2.30), page 8, is for the one-dimensional chain. These are different statements from the four-neighbor interpolation printed here. The energy conventions match after using \(J=1/2\), since a disagreement indicator is \((1-s_xs_y)/2\).

There is substantial valid counterevidence at the endpoints. For \(p=1\) and \(p=0\), expanding the NE and SW exponentials into constants, nearest-neighbor products and diagonal products gives equal sums by translation on the torus; this is also the calculation in [GB], (4.6)–(4.8), page 13. For \(p=1/2\), detailed balance holds. Consequently a convex mixture of the endpoint rates preserves the Gibbs measure, but it is a different generator from the exponential of their weighted increments. The description of the \(p=1/2\) rate as heat-bath Glauber is also inaccurate in the usual convention: \(e^{-\beta\Delta H/2}\) and \(1/(1+e^{\beta\Delta H})\) are different rules, as [GB], (3.8) and (3.10), explicitly distinguish.
## Impact and repair boundary

The claimed invariant distribution is a core prerequisite for applying the Gibbs-based potential-theoretic derivation to this extension. Its failure is demonstrated even in the low-temperature regime, not merely at one moderate temperature. This warrants Major severity for the extension’s derivation and model identification. It does not, by itself, prove that the numerical barrier or every asymptotic assertion in Theorem 5.4 is false. One must either analyze the actual invariant law of the printed generator or explicitly change the generator and rederive its barrier, time normalization and prefactor. Neither correction is supplied by relabeling the rates. The main MH and purely cyclic models have separately valid invariant measures.

Problem 3 (P3: harmonicity is asserted on a nonharmonic boundary).  Severity: Minor, with a concrete repair of the proof domain. Lemma 9.10(1), page 55, asserts \(\phi_1=0\) on the indicated union of \(\overline{\mathcal Z}\)-sets outside \(\mathcal N(S)\). It fails to remove the regular-strip boundary \(\overline{\mathcal R}\), which overlaps \(\overline{\mathcal Z}\).
## Witness and proof

Use \(q=3,K=11,L=12\), \(a=1,b=2\), \(\mathcal P=\{\mathbf1\}\), \(\mathcal Q=\{\mathbf2\}\), and a width-two \(b\)-strip in rows 0 and 1. Let \(\sigma\) have one \(a\)-hole at \((0,0)\) and spin \(a\) outside the strip. Its hole set is a nonempty ladder tree (Proposition 6.17, page 29), so \[\sigma\in\overline{\mathcal B}^{a,b}_0
 \subset\overline{\mathcal Z}^{a,b}\cap\overline{\mathcal R}^{a,b}_2,
 \qquad \sigma\notin\mathcal N(S).\] Here \(\overline{\mathcal B}^{a,b}_0\) denotes the auxiliary target set called \(\overline B^{a,b}_0\) in Definition 8.13, not the bulk set. Membership follows also from Lemma D.4, pages 73–74, and the disjointness of the auxiliary targets. The other ground-state neighborhoods are excluded by the edge-region decomposition.

Write \(f=f_{\overline A,\overline B}\). Definition 9.2, page 51, gives \[\widetilde h(\sigma)=1-\frac e\kappa,\qquad
 \widetilde h(\zeta)=1-\frac e\kappa+\frac e\kappa f(\zeta)
 \quad(\zeta\in\overline{\mathcal Z}^{a,b}).\] The energy of \(\sigma\) is \(24\). Exactly four outgoing rotations have orbit height at most \(\Gamma=26\): filling the hole, of height 25, and rotating the \(b\)-spins at \((1,0),(10,0),(0,1)\) to 3, each of height 26. Filling the hole leaves \(\widetilde h\) unchanged. Each other destination has \(f\geq0\), and at least one has \(f>0\): after rotating \((1,0)\) to 3, rotate it to 1 and extend the contiguous hole interval along row 0 to length \(K-1\). All intervening orbit heights are 26. The final configuration belongs to \(\overline A\), because closing the last remaining \(b\)-site has orbit height 25 and leads to a subbarrier path to \(\mathbf a\). This path avoids \(\overline B\), so it has strictly positive auxiliary-chain probability.

Equation reference: eq:boundary. The definition of \(\phi_1\), page 53, sums over destinations in \(\widehat{\mathcal N}(S)\), not just edges of height at most \(\Gamma\). This distinction was checked explicitly. The additional 21 outgoing destinations of energy at most 26 have minimum incident orbit height 27; they cannot belong to \(\widehat{\mathcal N}(S)\). All remaining destinations have energy above 26. Thus no omitted term changes the sign, and \[
 \phi_1(\sigma)
 =-\frac{e\,e^{-\Gamma\beta}}{\kappa Z_\beta}
       \sum_{j=1}^{3}f(\zeta_j)<0.\] Full local energy enumeration and the explicit positive-probability path are retained in the independent checks.
## Dependency and repair

Restrict the harmonicity claim to the auxiliary interior, excluding both \(\mathcal N(S)\) and the regular-strip boundary. The latter must be handled through the aggregate cancellation of Lemma 9.9 and the potential flatness of Lemma 9.5. The final proof on page 56 already invokes those two ingredients. For a regular orbit, \(\sum\phi_1=0\), each term is \(O(e^{-\Gamma\beta})\), and the potential varies by \(o(1)\); hence its total weighted contribution is \(o(e^{-\Gamma\beta})\) on the fixed finite lattice. This supplies the needed repair. A false local lemma is established, while the principal \(H^1\)-approximation conclusion is not refuted.

Problem 4 (P4: missing exclusions in quantifiers and projection domains).  Severity: Minor. The relevant statements have an evident intended restricted domain, but their literal domains include counterexamples.

First, Theorems 3.1–3.2, page 8, need distinct ground states in their pairwise formulas: (3.7) gives \(\Phi(\mathbf a,\mathbf a)=0\), and \({\mathbb E}_{\mathbf a}\tau_{\mathbf a}=0\), whereas their displayed barrier and prefactor are positive. Similarly, the disjointness clauses in Proposition 6.4, page 21, and Propositions 6.16 and 8.12, pages 27 and 49, require the appropriate distinct labels; a nonempty set does not have empty intersection with itself. In the three-label clauses, the endpoint labels must be distinct and \(a\notin\{b,c\}\). Definition 8.1, page 44, already implicitly excludes \(a=b\) by requiring \(1\leq r\leq q-1\). These qualifications preserve the intended inter-well statements.

Second, Proposition 6.21, page 31, excludes only the single configuration \(\mathbf a\), although its projection \(\Pi\) collapses all of \(\mathcal N(\mathbf a)\). Take the \(11\times12\) torus, \(q=3\), and let \(\eta_1\) be the all-1 state with one 2-spin at \((0,0)\), and \(\eta_2\) have an additional 2-spin at \((1,0)\). Their energies are 4 and 6. Both are distinct from \(\mathbf1\), lie in \(\mathcal N(\mathbf1)\), and are MH neighbors. Nevertheless, \[r(\Pi\eta_1,\Pi\eta_2)=r(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)=0,\qquad
 \mu_\beta(\eta_1)r_\beta(\eta_1,\eta_2)
       =Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-6\beta}>0.\] Thus (6.15) fails on the stated domain; (6.16) has the same issue. Require the uncollapsed inputs to lie outside \(\mathcal N(\mathbf a)\), equivalently \(\Pi\eta_i\ne\mathbf a\). The proof on page 66 and the applications to noncollapsed graph vertices already use that interpretation. These are domain repairs, not evidence against the intended graph approximation.

Problem 5 (P5: the trace-capacity multiplier in (D.8)).  Severity: Minor. In the proof of Proposition 8.14, page 74, the trace is explicitly taken on the unbarred vertex set \(\mathcal Z_\ell^{a,b}\). Equation (D.8), page 75, instead multiplies its capacity by \(|\overline A_\ell^{a,b}|+|\overline B_\ell^{a,b}|\).

Equation reference: eq:trace. For a chain uniform on \(\overline V\), its trace on \(Z\subset\overline V\) is uniform on \(Z\). For disjoint \(A,B\subset Z\), the exact identity is \[
 |\overline V|\,\operatorname{cap}_{\overline V}(A,B)
       =|Z|\,\operatorname{cap}_{Z}(A,B).\] Indeed, tracing preserves the equilibrium potential on \(Z\) and the boundary flux after multiplication by the stationary mass \(\mu(Z)=|Z|/|\overline V|\). Applying the boundary-flux definition of capacity proves [eq:trace] (#eq:trace) directly.

Here \(Z\) has interior vertices. For example, two adjacent \(a\)-holes in the width-two strip form a ladder tree, are not a single-hole \(B\) configuration, and are not adjacent by an energy-lowering flip to \(\mathcal N^{\rm MH}(\mathbf a)\); Lemma D.4 therefore excludes membership in \(A\). Capacity is positive, so the two different multipliers cannot give the same value.

Replace the printed multiplier by \(|\mathcal Z_\ell^{a,b}|\). A possible alternative is to define a further trace on \(A\cup B\), but that is not the trace defined in the preceding paragraph. The corrected cardinality and unit-rate graph are still independent of the spin labels, so the proof of label independence survives. The separate path-energy argument proving \(e_0<2\), later on page 75, does not use the erroneous multiplier and remains valid.

Problem 6 (P6: local path-index and energy bookkeeping).  Severity: Minor. Three explicitly repairable proof steps require correction; none supplies a counterexample to the associated asymptotic conclusion.

Arbitrary path length. Proposition 8.5 allows a path \((\omega_n)_{n=0}^N\), but its proof (D.1) and the threshold-index choice on page 69 use \(KL\); the same restriction recurs on page 71. General paths can include arbitrarily many local cycles before reaching the threshold number of \(b\)-spins. Replace the index ranges by \(0,\ldots,N\) and \(0,\ldots,N-1\), as applicable. The count changes by at most one at each step and goes from 0 to \(KL\), so the last threshold crossing exists over the full path. The subsequent local configuration argument is unaffected. This is an invalid indexing restriction, not a constructed subbarrier transition.

Maximum rather than minimum. In the last estimate for Lemma 7.16, page 43, the condition on a nonzero test-function difference must use \(\max\{H(\eta),H(\xi)\}\geq\Gamma\), not the printed minimum. A width-one strip of energy \(2K\) is in \(\mathcal N(\mathbf a)\); adding a one-site protuberance gives a neighboring edge state of energy \(2K+2=\Gamma\). The latter has positive probability to grow to the width-two strip before returning to \(\mathcal N(\mathbf a)\), so its edge potential is strictly below the neighborhood value 1. The minimum energy is \(2K<\Gamma\). The intended estimate follows directly from the MH conductance \(Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta\max(H(\eta),H(\xi))}\), so changing minimum to maximum repairs the bound.

A negligible term is not exactly zero. Appendix C, page 68, assumes \(q=2\) and finally equates the whole-space gateway energy sum to its restriction to \(\mathcal E\cup\mathcal B\). On the \(11\times12\) torus, take a regular width-three 2-strip in a 1-background. Its energy is 22, and flipping an interior 2-spin with four 2-neighbors raises the energy to 26. The destination is outside \(\widehat{\mathcal N}(S)=\mathcal E\cup\mathcal B\), since the MH barrier is 24, and has test value 1 by Definition 7.2. The strip has test value strictly below 1. This crossing contributes a strictly positive term \(Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-26\beta}(1-\widetilde h(\eta))^2\). The exact equality is therefore false. All such crossing terms are \(O(e^{-(\Gamma+1)\beta})\) at fixed volume by Lemma 6.5, page 21; adding this remainder preserves Proposition C.1. The appendix itself states that this proposition is not needed for the present paper.
# Positive checks, coverage and limits

The core approximation mechanism was checked independently of the extension findings. On a finite chain, \(D_\beta(f)=\langle f,-L_\beta f\rangle_{\mu_\beta}\) is a nonnegative quadratic form even without reversibility. If \(h\) is harmonic off the boundary and \(\widetilde h=h\) on that boundary, stationarity and harmonicity give \[D_\beta(h-\widetilde h)
       =D_\beta(\widetilde h)-\langle h,-L_\beta\widetilde h\rangle_{\mu_\beta}.\] Thus the use of the \(H^1\) seminorm and the energy comparison in Sections 4 and 9 does not secretly require self-adjointness. The finite-graph capacity/mean-hitting-time and trace-rate algebra was checked with the paper’s probability normalization; in particular the factor \(q\) cancels in the stated complete-graph capacity constant.

The MH and pure cyclic invariant-measure identities were verified directly. The local cyclic orbit has constant Gibbs-weighted rate, and reversing an edge by the rest of its orbit preserves its height. The canonical strip calculation was independently enumerated for all 132 updates of an \(11\times12\), three-spin path: every case of (8.2) agreed, with maximum cyclic height 26 and MH height 24. This is a check of that exact path, not a computational proof of the global minimum barrier.

The lower-barrier arguments, ladder-tree characterization, edge/bulk decomposition, test-function boundary matching, and fixed-volume higher-energy error estimates were read through their appendix proofs. In the bulk, the MH endpoint increments and the cyclic \(K-2\) interpolation produce the indicated harmonic cancellations. The auxiliary path lower bounds for capacity, including the \(K\) edge-disjoint paths in the final proof of \(e_0<2\), were checked by Cauchy–Schwarz. The regular-orbit aggregate cancellation, rather than pointwise zero flux, is the relevant mechanism at the overlap identified in Problem Problem 3 (#prob:p3).

Some historical results cited for general metastability and cycle estimates were not re-proved in their complete original generality. The finite-chain identities actually used above were independently derived, and the cited directed-Ising dependency was checked in its original PDF. The open-boundary extension summarized in Section 3.5 has no complete proof in the reviewed text; no new full open-boundary proof is claimed here. No author program was executed, and no absence of code is counted as a defect.

The assessment is Major for the two Section 5 issues, with the stated local Minor repairs elsewhere. Problem Problem 1 (#prob:p1) proves that the assertions of Theorem 5.2 are mutually inconsistent. Problem Problem 2 (#prob:p2) disproves its extension’s invariant-measure assertion and invalidates the proposed Gibbs-based derivation, while leaving the final numerical assertions of Theorem 5.4 unadjudicated. Neither finding proves failure of the whole paper or of the intended principal MH and purely cyclic conclusions.
# Supporting checks

The exact reviewed source SHA256 is \[\text{\texttt{8b64f17526ff3dc8f7bddabf9f01d33ddc68dd5ab6ce0bb9bda483246c344d63}}.\] The acquired reference [GB] is arXiv:0911.4011v1, 20 November 2009, 19 pages, SHA256 \[\text{\texttt{a0143fa18412450a939077df1865b5f1ace11b5c7042453182e84e017e8ff088}}.\] The paper-owned verification directory retains the original source manifest, three independently written calculation scripts and their actual outputs, full source text, per-problem evidence, selected native-image inspection records, failed publisher response, and compiler records. The independent arithmetic uses exact rational numbers, integer edge counts and symbolic algebra; no simulation uncertainty is involved in the displayed counterexamples. Rendering, acquisition and manifest parsing are not counted as scientific reading or image viewing.

All substantive interpretation, proof checks and actual source/report image inspections belong to the root scientific executor of this assignment. Native helpers performed bounded acquisition, metadata and binding tasks only. Runtime self-report and the controller’s UI observation are retained separately; backend equivalence is not certified. This initial report is not independent acceptance. Scientific decision remains pending and the human-review list is empty.

claim: Recorded check: The directed Ising rates printed in Section5.2 do not preserve the Gibbs measure

q=2 encoded as +/-1; K=11,L=12 periodic torus; unordered disagreement Hamiltonian. All positive spins except negative sites (4,5),(5,5),(5,6),(6,5). Printed c_p=exp[-beta(p A+(1-p)B)] with A=NE energy increment,B=SW increment. Any beta>0 and0<p<1,p!=1/2; explicit rational check p=1/3,beta=3log2.
analysis: Severity: Major, localized to Section 5.2. Pages 19–20 define one exponential of a weighted directional energy increment and assert that \(\mu_\beta\) is invariant for every \(p\in[0,1]\). That assertion is false for the displayed generator and Hamiltonian.

The claimed invariant distribution is a core prerequisite for applying the Gibbs-based potential-theoretic derivation to this extension. Its failure is demonstrated even in the low-temperature regime, not merely at one moderate temperature. This warrants Major severity for the extension’s derivation and model identification. It does not, by itself, prove that the numerical barrier or every asymptotic assertion in Theorem 5.4 is false. One must either analyze the actual invariant law of the printed generator or explicitly change the generator and rederive its barrier, time normalization and prefactor. Neither correction is supplied by relabeling the rates. The main MH and purely cyclic models have separately valid invariant measures.
result: The source rates contain no positive part and no sum of exponentials; both details were checked in the page image. Changing the temperature convention or multiplying all rates by a common positive factor cannot make the nonzero balance residual vanish.

The cited reference [19], Godrèche–Bray [GB], Section 3.3, equations (3.13)–(3.14), pages 10–11, treats the purely NE directed rate and a three-neighbor extension. Its exponential interpolation (2.30), page 8, is for the one-dimensional chain. These are different statements from the four-neighbor interpolation printed here. The energy conventions match after using \(J=1/2\), since a disagreement indicator is \((1-s_xs_y)/2\).

There is substantial valid counterevidence at the endpoints. For \(p=1\) and \(p=0\), expanding the NE and SW exponentials into constants, nearest-neighbor products and diagonal products gives equal sums by translation on the torus; this is also the calculation in [GB], (4.6)–(4.8), page 13. For \(p=1/2\), detailed balance holds. Consequently a convex mixture of the endpoint rates preserves the Gibbs measure, but it is a different generator from the exponential of their weighted increments. The description of the \(p=1/2\) rate as heat-bath Glauber is also inaccurate in the usual convention: \(e^{-\beta\Delta H/2}\) and \(1/(1+e^{\beta\Delta H})\) are different rules, as [GB], (3.8) and (3.10), explicitly distinguish.

Recorded evidence: Decisive evidence: Full132-site increment multiplicities: (-2,0):2,(0,-2):1,(0,0):1,(0,2):4,(2,-2):1,(2,0):3,(2,2):120. With t=exp(beta p),u=exp(beta(1-p)), the incoming-minus-outgoing flux divided by mu(sigma) equals -(t^2-1)(t^2-u^2)(u^2-1)/(t^2u^2), nonzero in stated range. Rational out255/8,in/mu645/16,residual/mu135/16.

Recorded evidence: Counterevidence: p=0,1 satisfy global balance by translation; p=1/2 satisfies detailed balance. Reference[19] supports pure NE/SW rates; its exponential interpolation(2.30) is one-dimensional. A convex mixture of endpoint rates would be Gibbs-stationary but defines a different process. Usual heat-bath and exponential-half-energy rates differ.

repair.heading: Recorded correction and verification scope
paragraphs: Analyze the actual invariant measure of the printed rates, or explicitly change generator and rederive barrier/time scaling/prefactors. An exponential mixture cannot silently be read as a convex mixture of exponentials.

problems.title: Lemma9.10's pointwise harmonicity domain includes regular-strip boundary with nonzero flux
problems.source_location: Retained report, Problem 3: Problem 3 (P3: harmonicity is asserted on a nonharmonic boundary).
claim: Recorded check: Lemma9.10's pointwise harmonicity domain includes regular-strip boundary with nonzero flux

q=3,K=11,L=12,a=1,b=2,P={a},Q={b}. Width-two b strip rows0,1,one a-hole at(0,0); a elsewhere. Auxiliary targets A=Zbar intersect N(a), B=Zbar intersect regular-strip orbit. phi1 sums over all targets in Nhat(S), not only edges of height<=Gamma.
analysis: Severity: Minor, with a concrete repair of the proof domain. Lemma 9.10(1), page 55, asserts \(\phi_1=0\) on the indicated union of \(\overline{\mathcal Z}\)-sets outside \(\mathcal N(S)\). It fails to remove the regular-strip boundary \(\overline{\mathcal R}\), which overlaps \(\overline{\mathcal Z}\).

Use \(q=3,K=11,L=12\), \(a=1,b=2\), \(\mathcal P=\{\mathbf1\}\), \(\mathcal Q=\{\mathbf2\}\), and a width-two \(b\)-strip in rows 0 and 1. Let \(\sigma\) have one \(a\)-hole at \((0,0)\) and spin \(a\) outside the strip. Its hole set is a nonempty ladder tree (Proposition 6.17, page 29), so \[\sigma\in\overline{\mathcal B}^{a,b}_0
 \subset\overline{\mathcal Z}^{a,b}\cap\overline{\mathcal R}^{a,b}_2,
 \qquad \sigma\notin\mathcal N(S).\] Here \(\overline{\mathcal B}^{a,b}_0\) denotes the auxiliary target set called \(\overline B^{a,b}_0\) in Definition 8.13, not the bulk set. Membership follows also from Lemma D.4, pages 73–74, and the disjointness of the auxiliary targets. The other ground-state neighborhoods are excluded by the edge-region decomposition.

Write \(f=f_{\overline A,\overline B}\). Definition 9.2, page 51, gives \[\widetilde h(\sigma)=1-\frac e\kappa,\qquad
 \widetilde h(\zeta)=1-\frac e\kappa+\frac e\kappa f(\zeta)
 \quad(\zeta\in\overline{\mathcal Z}^{a,b}).\] The energy of \(\sigma\) is \(24\). Exactly four outgoing rotations have orbit height at most \(\Gamma=26\): filling the hole, of height 25, and rotating the \(b\)-spins at \((1,0),(10,0),(0,1)\) to 3, each of height 26. Filling the hole leaves \(\widetilde h\) unchanged. Each other destination has \(f\geq0\), and at least one has \(f>0\): after rotating \((1,0)\) to 3, rotate it to 1 and extend the contiguous hole interval along row 0 to length \(K-1\). All intervening orbit heights are 26. The final configuration belongs to \(\overline A\), because closing the last remaining \(b\)-site has orbit height 25 and leads to a subbarrier path to \(\mathbf a\). This path avoids \(\overline B\), so it has strictly positive auxiliary-chain probability.

Equation reference: eq:boundary. The definition of \(\phi_1\), page 53, sums over destinations in \(\widehat{\mathcal N}(S)\), not just edges of height at most \(\Gamma\). This distinction was checked explicitly. The additional 21 outgoing destinations of energy at most 26 have minimum incident orbit height 27; they cannot belong to \(\widehat{\mathcal N}(S)\). All remaining destinations have energy above 26. Thus no omitted term changes the sign, and \[
 \phi_1(\sigma)
 =-\frac{e\,e^{-\Gamma\beta}}{\kappa Z_\beta}
       \sum_{j=1}^{3}f(\zeta_j)<0.\] Full local energy enumeration and the explicit positive-probability path are retained in the independent checks.

Restrict the harmonicity claim to the auxiliary interior, excluding both \(\mathcal N(S)\) and the regular-strip boundary. The latter must be handled through the aggregate cancellation of Lemma 9.9 and the potential flatness of Lemma 9.5. The final proof on page 56 already invokes those two ingredients. For a regular orbit, \(\sum\phi_1=0\), each term is \(O(e^{-\Gamma\beta})\), and the potential varies by \(o(1)\); hence its total weighted contribution is \(o(e^{-\Gamma\beta})\) on the fixed finite lattice. This supplies the needed repair. A false local lemma is established, while the principal \(H^1\)-approximation conclusion is not refuted.
result: Recorded evidence: Decisive evidence: The witness is in B subset Zbar outside N(S), has H24, and exactly four outgoing rotations of orbit height<=26: fill hole (height25, same h) and three neighbor b->3 updates (height26). The test values of the latter equal h(sigma)+(e/kappa)f>=h(sigma), one strictly via a positive-probability path extending the hole tree to K-1 holes before B. All21 extra outgoing targets of H<=26 have minimum incident orbit height27 and are not in Nhat(S). Hence phi1(sigma)=-(e/(kappa Z_beta))exp(-26beta)sum_j f(zeta_j)<0.
Recorded evidence: Counterevidence: Lemma9.9 correctly provides aggregate cancellation, not pointwise zero; p.56 already invokes it with Lemma9.5's potential flatness.

repair.heading: Recorded correction and verification scope
paragraphs: Exclude regular-strip boundary as well as N(S) from Lemma9.10's harmonicity domain. Use sum phi1=0 plus each phi1=O(exp(-Gamma beta)) and o(1) potential variation on each regular orbit. Fixed finite volume makes the total o(exp(-Gamma beta)).

problems.title: Ground-state quantifiers and projected graph identities need excluded inputs
problems.source_location: Retained report, Problem 4: Problem 4 (P4: missing exclusions in quantifiers and projection domains).
claim: Recorded check: Ground-state quantifiers and projected graph identities need excluded inputs
Same periodic fixed lattice model, distinct/non-distinct labels treated literally. For projection witness q=3,K=11,L=12; one 2-spin or two adjacent 2-spins in all-1 background.
analysis: Severity: Minor. The relevant statements have an evident intended restricted domain, but their literal domains include counterexamples.

First, Theorems 3.1–3.2, page 8, need distinct ground states in their pairwise formulas: (3.7) gives \(\Phi(\mathbf a,\mathbf a)=0\), and \({\mathbb E}_{\mathbf a}\tau_{\mathbf a}=0\), whereas their displayed barrier and prefactor are positive. Similarly, the disjointness clauses in Proposition 6.4, page 21, and Propositions 6.16 and 8.12, pages 27 and 49, require the appropriate distinct labels; a nonempty set does not have empty intersection with itself. In the three-label clauses, the endpoint labels must be distinct and \(a\notin\{b,c\}\). Definition 8.1, page 44, already implicitly excludes \(a=b\) by requiring \(1\leq r\leq q-1\). These qualifications preserve the intended inter-well statements.

Second, Proposition 6.21, page 31, excludes only the single configuration \(\mathbf a\), although its projection \(\Pi\) collapses all of \(\mathcal N(\mathbf a)\). Take the \(11\times12\) torus, \(q=3\), and let \(\eta_1\) be the all-1 state with one 2-spin at \((0,0)\), and \(\eta_2\) have an additional 2-spin at \((1,0)\). Their energies are 4 and 6. Both are distinct from \(\mathbf1\), lie in \(\mathcal N(\mathbf1)\), and are MH neighbors. Nevertheless, \[r(\Pi\eta_1,\Pi\eta_2)=r(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)=0,\qquad
 \mu_\beta(\eta_1)r_\beta(\eta_1,\eta_2)
       =Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-6\beta}>0.\] Thus (6.15) fails on the stated domain; (6.16) has the same issue. Require the uncollapsed inputs to lie outside \(\mathcal N(\mathbf a)\), equivalently \(\Pi\eta_i\ne\mathbf a\). The proof on page 66 and the applications to noncollapsed graph vertices already use that interpretation. These are domain repairs, not evidence against the intended graph approximation.
result: Recorded evidence: Decisive evidence: Self communication height and self hitting time are0, not the asserted positive barrier/prefactor. A nonempty neighborhood/edge set cannot be disjoint from itself. For projection witness H=4 and6 and both states in N(a), Pi sends both to a so graph rate0, but original conductance=exp(-6beta)/Z_beta>0; hence broad printed domain in(6.15) fails.
Recorded evidence: Counterevidence: Inter-well context and Definition8.1 indicate intended distinct labels; proof and use of Proposition6.21 treat uncollapsed graph vertices outside N(a).

repair.heading: Recorded correction and verification scope
paragraphs: Require distinct pair labels, a not in{b,c} and b!=c for three-label clauses. Require inputs outside N(a), equivalently Pi eta_i!=a, in the graph identities.

problems.title: Equation(D.8) has the target-set size instead of the trace-state-space size
problems.source_location: Retained report, Problem 5: Problem 5 (P5: the trace-capacity multiplier in (D.8)).
claim: Recorded check: Equation(D.8) has the target-set size instead of the trace-state-space size
Finite auxiliary cyclic chain uniform on Vbar; trace on unbarred Z; disjoint nonempty A,B subsets of Z. K>=11 admits interior two-adjacent-hole ladder-tree configurations outside A union B.
analysis: Severity: Minor. In the proof of Proposition 8.14, page 74, the trace is explicitly taken on the unbarred vertex set \(\mathcal Z_\ell^{a,b}\). Equation (D.8), page 75, instead multiplies its capacity by \(|\overline A_\ell^{a,b}|+|\overline B_\ell^{a,b}|\).

Equation reference: eq:trace. For a chain uniform on \(\overline V\), its trace on \(Z\subset\overline V\) is uniform on \(Z\). For disjoint \(A,B\subset Z\), the exact identity is \[
 |\overline V|\,\operatorname{cap}_{\overline V}(A,B)
       =|Z|\,\operatorname{cap}_{Z}(A,B).\] Indeed, tracing preserves the equilibrium potential on \(Z\) and the boundary flux after multiplication by the stationary mass \(\mu(Z)=|Z|/|\overline V|\). Applying the boundary-flux definition of capacity proves [eq:trace] (#eq:trace) directly.

Here \(Z\) has interior vertices. For example, two adjacent \(a\)-holes in the width-two strip form a ladder tree, are not a single-hole \(B\) configuration, and are not adjacent by an energy-lowering flip to \(\mathcal N^{\rm MH}(\mathbf a)\); Lemma D.4 therefore excludes membership in \(A\). Capacity is positive, so the two different multipliers cannot give the same value.

Replace the printed multiplier by \(|\mathcal Z_\ell^{a,b}|\). A possible alternative is to define a further trace on \(A\cup B\), but that is not the trace defined in the preceding paragraph. The corrected cardinality and unit-rate graph are still independent of the spin labels, so the proof of label independence survives. The separate path-energy argument proving \(e_0<2\), later on page 75, does not use the erroneous multiplier and remains valid.
result: Recorded evidence: Decisive evidence: Conditioning the invariant measure on Z and preserving harmonic boundary flux yields |Vbar|cap_original(A,B)=|Z|cap_trace(A,B). Printed |A|+|B| is strictly smaller: two adjacent a-holes are an interior Z vertex by LemmaD.4 and have no lower-energy neighbor toward N_MH(a); capacity is positive.

Recorded evidence: Counterevidence: A further trace on A union B would permit that multiplier but is not the trace defined on p.74. Correct |Z| remains spin-label independent; the later path bound e0<2 uses original Dirichlet form independently of(D.8).

repair.heading: Recorded correction and verification scope
paragraphs: Replace factor by |Z|, or explicitly define and use a further trace on A union B with its capacity.

problems.title: Arbitrary path indices, MH energy bound and gateway restriction require local corrections
problems.source_location: Retained report, Problem 6: Problem 6 (P6: local path-index and energy bookkeeping).
claim: Recorded check: Arbitrary path indices, MH energy bound and gateway restriction require local corrections

Fixed finite periodic lattice, K,L>=11. Arbitrary directed path of lengthN, potentially with repeated local cycles. For MH minimum-energy example, width-one strip and one-site protuberance. AppendixC q=2; K11,L12 regular width-three strip and an interior spin flip.
analysis: Severity: Minor. Three explicitly repairable proof steps require correction; none supplies a counterexample to the associated asymptotic conclusion.

Arbitrary path length. Proposition 8.5 allows a path \((\omega_n)_{n=0}^N\), but its proof (D.1) and the threshold-index choice on page 69 use \(KL\); the same restriction recurs on page 71. General paths can include arbitrarily many local cycles before reaching the threshold number of \(b\)-spins. Replace the index ranges by \(0,\ldots,N\) and \(0,\ldots,N-1\), as applicable. The count changes by at most one at each step and goes from 0 to \(KL\), so the last threshold crossing exists over the full path. The subsequent local configuration argument is unaffected. This is an invalid indexing restriction, not a constructed subbarrier transition.

Maximum rather than minimum. In the last estimate for Lemma 7.16, page 43, the condition on a nonzero test-function difference must use \(\max\{H(\eta),H(\xi)\}\geq\Gamma\), not the printed minimum. A width-one strip of energy \(2K\) is in \(\mathcal N(\mathbf a)\); adding a one-site protuberance gives a neighboring edge state of energy \(2K+2=\Gamma\). The latter has positive probability to grow to the width-two strip before returning to \(\mathcal N(\mathbf a)\), so its edge potential is strictly below the neighborhood value 1. The minimum energy is \(2K<\Gamma\). The intended estimate follows directly from the MH conductance \(Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta\max(H(\eta),H(\xi))}\), so changing minimum to maximum repairs the bound.

A negligible term is not exactly zero. Appendix C, page 68, assumes \(q=2\) and finally equates the whole-space gateway energy sum to its restriction to \(\mathcal E\cup\mathcal B\). On the \(11\times12\) torus, take a regular width-three 2-strip in a 1-background. Its energy is 22, and flipping an interior 2-spin with four 2-neighbors raises the energy to 26. The destination is outside \(\widehat{\mathcal N}(S)=\mathcal E\cup\mathcal B\), since the MH barrier is 24, and has test value 1 by Definition 7.2. The strip has test value strictly below 1. This crossing contributes a strictly positive term \(Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-26\beta}(1-\widetilde h(\eta))^2\). The exact equality is therefore false. All such crossing terms are \(O(e^{-(\Gamma+1)\beta})\) at fixed volume by Lemma 6.5, page 21; adding this remainder preserves Proposition C.1. The appendix itself states that this proposition is not needed for the present paper.
result: Recorded evidence: Decisive evidence: General path indices range toN, notKL; arbitrary low local cycles can precede any transition and delay threshold counts. In MH an H=2K neighborhood strip neighbors an H=2K+2 edge state with different test value; min<Gamma while max=Gamma. For AppendixC the H22 width-three strip neighbors an H26 outside state with h=1 and positive crossing energy exp(-26beta)(1-h(strip))^2/Z, so the restricted and whole-space sums are not exactly equal.

Recorded evidence: Counterevidence: Replacing indices byN restores threshold existence; MH conductance uses maximum endpoint energy and supplies intended O(exp(-Gamma beta)) bound; crossing remainder is O(exp(-(Gamma+1)beta)) at fixed volume. AppendixC explicitly not needed in the current paper.

repair.heading: Recorded correction and verification scope
paragraphs: Use actual path lengthN throughout; replace minimum by maximum; retain a higher-energy remainder in AppendixC's final equality.

report: Abstract: The reviewed version contains two independently demonstrated defects in the written strict-monotonicity argument: the passage from split edges to successor states loses multiplicities and, at positive parameter increment, changes the evolution of untouched herds; a subsequent reciprocal bound uses a minimum where a maximum is required. Exact local generator calculations corroborate the first finding. A separate discretization error omits a terminal time interval in the birth-count estimate. These are errors in displayed identities or proof steps, not counterexamples to the final theorems. Explicit repairs are given within the checked scope. Scientific adjudication remains pending.
Author: AI-assisted technical review

Title: Technical Review of
The Contact Process on Dynamic Regular Graphs:
Subcritical Phase and Monotonicity
# Paper identity and scope

The paper is by Bruno Schapira and Daniel Valesin, The Annals of Probability 53(2) (2025), 753–796, DOI 10.1214/24-AOP1721 (https://doi.org/10.1214/24-AOP1721). The reviewed file is the 44-page publisher-formatted version of record acquired from the author’s website. Printed page \(p\) is physical PDF page \(p-752\). All page locators below refer to printed pages unless explicitly stated otherwise.

The complete extracted text, including the appendix and references, was read. The most intensive independent checks concern Definitions 2.1–2.4, the particle-count generator, Proposition 3.7, Lemma 3.8, the use of those results in Proposition 3.6, and the time partition in Corollary 3.15. The source pages supporting these findings were also viewed as rendered images. Reading the other proofs is not represented as an independent certification of every argument or of the external results they cite.

The author publication list and arXiv version history were consulted for correction and version context on 29 October 2026. The inspected arXiv record 2309.17040 lists a single 65-page version dated 29 September 2023; it is not the reviewed 44-page journal file. The inspected author entry links the journal-formatted article. No relevant correction was located in this bounded check. This does not establish that no correction exists elsewhere. No author code was executed.
# Definitions and operative assumptions

Fix an integer \(d\geq3\), birth rate \(\lambda>0\), and splitting rate \(v>0\). A herd shape \(A\) is any finite nonempty subset of the infinite \(d\)-regular tree. It need not be connected (Definition 2.1, p. 756). A state \(\xi\in\mathcal S\) is a finite multiset of such shapes. For an edge \(e\), write \(A_{e,1},A_{e,2}\) for the portions on the two sides of \(e\). An edge is active precisely when both portions are nonempty.

Equation reference: gen. Definition 2.3, p. 757, gives a death rate of one per particle, birth rate \(\lambda\) per occupied-neighbor arrow to an unoccupied site of the same herd, and split rate \(v\) per active edge per herd copy. Different herds evolve independently, even when their spatial locations overlap. Let \(X(\xi)\) be the total particle count, \(H(\xi)\) the total number of occupied adjacent pairs within herds, and \(\mathcal E(\xi)\) the active-edge count with herd multiplicities. Let \(L_v\) denote this generator and put \[S_v(t)\xi=\mathbb E_{\lambda,v}[X_t\mid\Xi_0=\xi],
 \qquad F_v(t)=S_v(t)\delta_{\{o\}}.\] Splitting preserves \(X\). Counting the available birth arrows gives \[
 L_vX=(d\lambda-1)X-2\lambda H .\] The paper’s pure-birth domination and Corollary 2.3 provide finite moments on bounded time intervals. Proposition 2.7 implies \(F_v(t+s)\leq F_v(t)F_v(s)\). These facts supply the integrability and positivity used below; in particular, \(F_v(t)\geq e^{-t}>0\), by survival of the initial particle.
# Errors in the derivative kernel

Problem 1 (Split multiplicity and the finite-increment kernel).  The successor-state rewriting in (28)–(29), pp. 769–770, and the associated first-separation calculation in Lemma 3.10, p. 771, do not follow from the stated definitions. Severity: Major, as an invalid step in a core derivation; no false final theorem is established.
## Original assertions

Equation reference: g. For every \(\xi\in\mathcal S\) and \(t\geq0\), (20) defines \[
 g_v(\xi,t)=\sum_A\xi(A)\sum_{e\text{ active in }A}
 \bigl[S_v(t)(\delta_{A_{e,1}}+\delta_{A_{e,2}})
                  -S_v(t)\delta_A\bigr].\] Equation (27) replaces the first \(v\) in each bracket by \(v+\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon>0\), and calls the result \(g_{v,\varepsilon}\). Definition 3.2 defines \(G(\xi)\) as a set of successor configurations and, for the shape \(A\) split to obtain \(\xi'\), sets \(m(\xi,\xi')=\xi(A)\). Equations (28) and (29) assert, respectively, that the preceding edge sums equal \[\sum_{\xi'\in G(\xi)}m(\xi,\xi')
       [S_v(t)\xi'-S_v(t)\xi],\qquad
 \sum_{\xi'\in G(\xi)}m(\xi,\xi')
       [S_{v+\varepsilon}(t)\xi'-S_v(t)\xi].\] There are two distinct failures.
## Two active edges can have the same successor

Let \(a,b,c\) be three successive vertices of the tree and \(A=\{a,c\}\), \(\xi=\delta_A\). Both \(ab\) and \(bc\) are active. They give the same successor \(\xi'=\delta_{\{a\}}+\delta_{\{c\}}\). Thus \(G(\xi)\) has one element and the printed \(m\) is one, whereas Definition 2.3 gives the transition \(\xi\to\xi'\) total rate \(2v\). Likewise the extra split clock at rate increment \(\varepsilon\) gives first-order probability \(2\varepsilon s+o(s)\), rather than \(\varepsilon s+o(s)\).

This state satisfies all the definitions. It also occurs with positive probability starting from a singleton: require two consecutive births along \(a,b,c\), then death of \(b\), with no intervening split or other event. All prescribed transition rates are positive and the finite list of holding rates is finite. Restricting attention to the actual process started at \(\delta_{\{o\}}\) therefore does not remove the example.

Equation reference: d2. The discrepancy in (28) is substantive even as an identity of expectations. Set \[D(t)=S_v(t)\xi'-S_v(t)\xi.\] Both configurations have \(X=2,H=0\), so \(D(0)=D'(0)=0\). At \(\xi\), birth at the middle vertex has rate \(2\lambda\) and adds two occupied adjacent pairs; the other \(2(d-1)\) birth arrows each add one. At \(\xi'\), there are \(2d\) arrows, each adding one within its own herd. Consequently \[L_vH(\xi)=2(d+1)\lambda,\qquad L_vH(\xi')=2d\lambda .\] Applying [gen] (#gen) twice yields \[
 D''(0)=4\lambda^2,\qquad
 D(t)=2\lambda^2t^2+o(t^2)>0
 \quad\text{for all sufficiently small }t>0.\] The edge definition is \(2D(t)\); the printed state sum is \(D(t)\).

The use of right derivatives at zero is justified by the finite local transition lists and the bounded-time moment domination: the finite generator iterations here have polynomial growth in the relevant counts, and the finite-step expansion can be localized and then dominated. An independent exact rational enumeration confirms [d2] (#d2). For \(d=3,\lambda=1/6,v=1\), its results are \[\begin{array}{c|rrr}
 &X&L_vX&L_v^2X\\ \hline
 \delta_{\{a,c\}}&2&-1&1/18\\
 \delta_{\{a\}}+\delta_{\{c\}}&2&-1&1/6
\end{array}\] and hence \(D''(0)=1/9\), \(D(t)=t^2/18+o(t^2)\). The enumeration aggregates all elementary transition rates, checks full degree at every evaluated vertex, and uses rational arithmetic. It is a local generator calculation, not a simulation or a numerical approximation to a large-time theorem.
## Untouched herds do not cancel at positive increment

The exact enumeration with \(d=3,\lambda=1/6,v=1,\varepsilon=1\) returns \[\begin{array}{c|rrrr}
 &F(0)&F'(0)&F''(0)&F'''(0)\\ \hline
 v=1&1&-1/2&1/12&43/72\\
 v=2&1&-1/2&1/12&55/72
 \end{array}\] and [untouched] (#untouched) is \(t^3/36+o(t^3)>0\). Definition 3.3 evolves the whole second process with parameter \(v+\varepsilon\) after separation. Thus the omitted singleton term is also present in the actual conditional calculation used in Lemma 3.10.
## Alternative readings, correction, and impact

Interpreting \(G\) as a multiset indexed by elementary split events would address the first problem, but that is a change to the explicit set definition, not the printed identity. Assuming connected shapes contradicts Definition 2.1 and is not invariant under deaths. Neither reading addresses the untouched-herd term at \(\varepsilon>0\).

Equation reference: correctkernel. One may retain edge indexing throughout and use \[
 \widetilde g_{v,\varepsilon}(\xi,t)
 =\sum_A\xi(A)\sum_{e\text{ active in }A}
 \left[S_{v+\varepsilon}(t)
    \bigl(\xi-\delta_A+\delta_{A_{e,1}}+\delta_{A_{e,2}}\bigr)
       -S_v(t)\xi\right].\] Alternatively the correct successor multiplicity is the total number of elementary split events, including copies, that yield that successor. At \(\varepsilon=0\), additivity cancels untouched herds in [correctkernel] (#correctkernel), giving exactly [g] (#g). For \(0\leq t\leq T\), pure-birth domination gives the uniform bound \[|\widetilde g_{v,\varepsilon}(\xi,t)|
 \leq 2e^{d\lambda T}X(\xi)\mathcal E(\xi).\] This supplies the same kind of integrability needed in Lemmas 3.9–3.11 and the appendix, pp. 793–794. Finite-time parameter continuity gives \(\widetilde g_{v,\varepsilon}\to g_v\); the extra-split separation probability tends to zero as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), by the bounded-time active-edge moment bound. These observations support replacing the finite-increment kernel and repeating the dominated-convergence argument.

The error affects the written proof of Proposition 3.7, which supplies the derivative estimate in Proposition 3.6 and hence Theorem 1.3. The subcritical characterization used in Section 3.4 also invokes Proposition 3.6. This is why the finding concerns a core derivation. Equation (20) itself has the correct elementary-event indexing; the limiting derivative formula and the final theorems have not been disproved. The proposed correction is a mathematical repair identified here, not an author-adopted correction or an independently accepted revision.
# The lower bound used for strict monotonicity

Problem 2 (Reciprocal extremum and a time-range restriction).  The last display in the proof of Lemma 3.8, p. 768, is false under the paper’s assumptions. The subsequent use of this lemma in Proposition 3.6, p. 769, also exceeds its time range. Severity: Major for the stated core lower-bound derivation; both identified steps admit local repairs.
## The false inequality and a counterexample

Equation reference: wrongmin. Lemma 3.8 compares one adjacent two-particle herd with two singleton herds, for all \(t\geq1\), asserting a gap at least \(\gamma F_v(t)\), where \(\gamma>0\) depends continuously on \(\lambda,v\). The coupling event in its proof first gives a lower bound involving \(\min_{t-1\leq s\leq t}F_v(s)\). The last display asserts \[
 \min_{t-1\leq s\leq t}F_v(s)
 \geq F_v(t)\left(\min_{0\leq r\leq1}F_v(r)\right)^{-1}.\] Take the admissible parameters \(d=3,\lambda=1/6,v=1\). Equation [gen] (#gen) and \(H\geq0\) imply \(F_v'(t)\leq-F_v(t)/2<0\). Consequently \(0<F_v(1)\leq e^{-1/2}<1\). At \(t=1\), the left side of [wrongmin] (#wrongmin) is \(F_v(1)\), while the right side is \(F_v(1)/F_v(1)=1\). This is a strict contradiction. It uses the actual process, not an arbitrary submultiplicative test function.
## Repair and its limits

The proof of Proposition 3.6 applies Lemma 3.8 with time argument \(t-s\) but integrates over \(1\leq s\leq t\). The lemma only permits \(t-s\geq1\). At \(s=t\), the split and unsplit particle counts agree, so a positive multiple of \(F_v(0)=1\) cannot be a valid gap. Restrict the integration to \(1\leq s\leq t-1\). For \(t\geq3\), its length \(t-2\) is at least \(t/3\); submultiplicativity gives \[F_v(s-1)F_v(t-s)\geq F_v(t-1)
       \geq F_v(t)/F_v(1).\] Accordingly the needed lower bound by a positive constant times \(tF_v(t)\) survives for all sufficiently large \(t\), with a changed constant. This is sufficient for the growth-index limit used there. Together with a corrected derivative proof, these checks preserve the specific strict-monotonicity strategy. They do not turn the erroneous display into a true one, nor certify all later arguments.
# A terminal interval in the birth-count estimate
Problem 3 (Floor versus ceiling in Corollary 3.15).  The union bound on p. 776 omits births in the final fractional time interval. Severity: Minor; the stated moment conclusion has a direct repair.

Under the section’s assumptions \(\lambda<\bar\lambda(v)\) and \(0<\varphi<1\), the proof fixes \(p\geq1\), \(x>1\), and \(t_x=(p+1)\log x/|\log\varphi|\). It bounds \(\mathbb P(N_{t_x}>x)\) by a sum over \(k=0,\ldots,\lfloor t_x\rfloor-1\) of events involving \(N_{k+1}-N_k\). For a concrete admissible choice of the time, set \(x=\exp(|\log\varphi|/[2(p+1)])\), so \(t_x=1/2\). The displayed sum is empty. Its left side is positive: the finite prescribed event of more than \(x\) successive births along a tree path before time \(1/2\), with no interfering death or split, has positive probability. All rates required for that event are positive and finite. This demonstrates a false bound, including within the stated \(x>1\) range.

Let \(m=\lceil t_x\rceil\). Monotonicity of \(N\) and the union bound instead give \[\mathbb P(N_{t_x}>x)
 \leq \sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\mathbb P(N_{k+1}-N_k>x/m)
 \leq m^{p+2}x^{-(p+1)}
       \sup_{t\geq0}\mathbb E[(N_{t+1}-N_t)^{p+1}].\] The supremum is the one controlled by (37) and (44). For \(x\geq e\), \(m=O(\log x)\), so the tail estimate needed to integrate the \(p\)th moment is unchanged in order. The bounded range of \(x\) contributes a finite amount. This repair establishes the specific partition step without altering the claim that all finite positive moments of the total birth count exist in the subcritical regime. It is not evidence against that conclusion.
# Assessment and coverage limits

The most consequential finding is the mismatch between the finite-increment coupling and its kernel. The counterexamples satisfy the stated domains, retain the exact positive parameters, and cannot be removed by an implicit connectivity convention. The reciprocal and partition errors are separately demonstrated and have explicit corrections. The identified repairs give substantial counterevidence against interpreting these defects as failures of the final theorems.

The review also checked the direction of the particle-count domination, the role of herd independence in expectation additivity, the submultiplicative inequality, and the dependence of the growth-index argument on the derivative formula. The finite-graph coupling in Section 4, all higher-moment constants, and the results imported from earlier papers were read but were not independently re-proved in full. No global correctness certificate is claimed.

problems.source_location: Retained report, Problem 1: Problem 1 (Split multiplicity and the finite-increment kernel).
claim: Fix an integer \(d\geq3\), birth rate \(\lambda>0\), and splitting rate \(v>0\). A herd shape \(A\) is any finite nonempty subset of the infinite \(d\)-regular tree. It need not be connected (Definition 2.1, p. 756). A state \(\xi\in\mathcal S\) is a finite multiset of such shapes. For an edge \(e\), write \(A_{e,1},A_{e,2}\) for the portions on the two sides of \(e\). An edge is active precisely when both portions are nonempty.

Equation reference: gen. Definition 2.3, p. 757, gives a death rate of one per particle, birth rate \(\lambda\) per occupied-neighbor arrow to an unoccupied site of the same herd, and split rate \(v\) per active edge per herd copy. Different herds evolve independently, even when their spatial locations overlap. Let \(X(\xi)\) be the total particle count, \(H(\xi)\) the total number of occupied adjacent pairs within herds, and \(\mathcal E(\xi)\) the active-edge count with herd multiplicities. Let \(L_v\) denote this generator and put \[S_v(t)\xi=\mathbb E_{\lambda,v}[X_t\mid\Xi_0=\xi],
 \qquad F_v(t)=S_v(t)\delta_{\{o\}}.\] Splitting preserves \(X\). Counting the available birth arrows gives \[
 L_vX=(d\lambda-1)X-2\lambda H .\] The paper’s pure-birth domination and Corollary 2.3 provide finite moments on bounded time intervals. Proposition 2.7 implies \(F_v(t+s)\leq F_v(t)F_v(s)\). These facts supply the integrability and positivity used below; in particular, \(F_v(t)\geq e^{-t}>0\), by survival of the initial particle.
Successor-state sums with m(xi,xi')=xi(A) equal elementary-edge sums; positive-epsilon equation(29) cancels untouched herds.
d integer>=3; lambda>0; v>0; epsilon>0 for finite increment; finite nonempty herd shapes, not necessarily connected; finite herd multiset; t>=0.
analysis: The successor-state rewriting in (28)–(29), pp. 769–770, and the associated first-separation calculation in Lemma 3.10, p. 771, do not follow from the stated definitions. Severity: Major, as an invalid step in a core derivation; no false final theorem is established.

Equation reference: g. For every \(\xi\in\mathcal S\) and \(t\geq0\), (20) defines \[
 g_v(\xi,t)=\sum_A\xi(A)\sum_{e\text{ active in }A}
 \bigl[S_v(t)(\delta_{A_{e,1}}+\delta_{A_{e,2}})
                  -S_v(t)\delta_A\bigr].\] Equation (27) replaces the first \(v\) in each bracket by \(v+\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon>0\), and calls the result \(g_{v,\varepsilon}\). Definition 3.2 defines \(G(\xi)\) as a set of successor configurations and, for the shape \(A\) split to obtain \(\xi'\), sets \(m(\xi,\xi')=\xi(A)\). Equations (28) and (29) assert, respectively, that the preceding edge sums equal \[\sum_{\xi'\in G(\xi)}m(\xi,\xi')
       [S_v(t)\xi'-S_v(t)\xi],\qquad
 \sum_{\xi'\in G(\xi)}m(\xi,\xi')
       [S_{v+\varepsilon}(t)\xi'-S_v(t)\xi].\] There are two distinct failures.

Let \(a,b,c\) be three successive vertices of the tree and \(A=\{a,c\}\), \(\xi=\delta_A\). Both \(ab\) and \(bc\) are active. They give the same successor \(\xi'=\delta_{\{a\}}+\delta_{\{c\}}\). Thus \(G(\xi)\) has one element and the printed \(m\) is one, whereas Definition 2.3 gives the transition \(\xi\to\xi'\) total rate \(2v\). Likewise the extra split clock at rate increment \(\varepsilon\) gives first-order probability \(2\varepsilon s+o(s)\), rather than \(\varepsilon s+o(s)\).

This state satisfies all the definitions. It also occurs with positive probability starting from a singleton: require two consecutive births along \(a,b,c\), then death of \(b\), with no intervening split or other event. All prescribed transition rates are positive and the finite list of holding rates is finite. Restricting attention to the actual process started at \(\delta_{\{o\}}\) therefore does not remove the example.

Equation reference: d2. The discrepancy in (28) is substantive even as an identity of expectations. Set \[D(t)=S_v(t)\xi'-S_v(t)\xi.\] Both configurations have \(X=2,H=0\), so \(D(0)=D'(0)=0\). At \(\xi\), birth at the middle vertex has rate \(2\lambda\) and adds two occupied adjacent pairs; the other \(2(d-1)\) birth arrows each add one. At \(\xi'\), there are \(2d\) arrows, each adding one within its own herd. Consequently \[L_vH(\xi)=2(d+1)\lambda,\qquad L_vH(\xi')=2d\lambda .\] Applying [gen] (#gen) twice yields \[
 D''(0)=4\lambda^2,\qquad
 D(t)=2\lambda^2t^2+o(t^2)>0
 \quad\text{for all sufficiently small }t>0.\] The edge definition is \(2D(t)\); the printed state sum is \(D(t)\).

The use of right derivatives at zero is justified by the finite local transition lists and the bounded-time moment domination: the finite generator iterations here have polynomial growth in the relevant counts, and the finite-step expansion can be localized and then dominated. An independent exact rational enumeration confirms [d2] (#d2). For \(d=3,\lambda=1/6,v=1\), its results are \[\begin{array}{c|rrr}
 &X&L_vX&L_v^2X\\ \hline
 \delta_{\{a,c\}}&2&-1&1/18\\
 \delta_{\{a\}}+\delta_{\{c\}}&2&-1&1/6
\end{array}\] and hence \(D''(0)=1/9\), \(D(t)=t^2/18+o(t^2)\). The enumeration aggregates all elementary transition rates, checks full degree at every evaluated vertex, and uses rational arithmetic. It is a local generator calculation, not a simulation or a numerical approximation to a large-time theorem.

The exact enumeration with \(d=3,\lambda=1/6,v=1,\varepsilon=1\) returns \[\begin{array}{c|rrrr}
 &F(0)&F'(0)&F''(0)&F'''(0)\\ \hline
 v=1&1&-1/2&1/12&43/72\\
 v=2&1&-1/2&1/12&55/72
 \end{array}\] and [untouched] (#untouched) is \(t^3/36+o(t^3)>0\). Definition 3.3 evolves the whole second process with parameter \(v+\varepsilon\) after separation. Thus the omitted singleton term is also present in the actual conditional calculation used in Lemma 3.10.
result: Interpreting \(G\) as a multiset indexed by elementary split events would address the first problem, but that is a change to the explicit set definition, not the printed identity. Assuming connected shapes contradicts Definition 2.1 and is not invariant under deaths. Neither reading addresses the untouched-herd term at \(\varepsilon>0\).

Equation reference: correctkernel. One may retain edge indexing throughout and use \[
 \widetilde g_{v,\varepsilon}(\xi,t)
 =\sum_A\xi(A)\sum_{e\text{ active in }A}
 \left[S_{v+\varepsilon}(t)
    \bigl(\xi-\delta_A+\delta_{A_{e,1}}+\delta_{A_{e,2}}\bigr)
       -S_v(t)\xi\right].\] Alternatively the correct successor multiplicity is the total number of elementary split events, including copies, that yield that successor. At \(\varepsilon=0\), additivity cancels untouched herds in [correctkernel] (#correctkernel), giving exactly [g] (#g). For \(0\leq t\leq T\), pure-birth domination gives the uniform bound \[|\widetilde g_{v,\varepsilon}(\xi,t)|
 \leq 2e^{d\lambda T}X(\xi)\mathcal E(\xi).\] This supplies the same kind of integrability needed in Lemmas 3.9–3.11 and the appendix, pp. 793–794. These observations support replacing the finite-increment kernel and repeating the dominated-convergence argument.

The error affects the written proof of Proposition 3.7, which supplies the derivative estimate in Proposition 3.6 and hence Theorem 1.3. The subcritical characterization used in Section 3.4 also invokes Proposition 3.6. This is why the finding concerns a core derivation. Equation (20) itself has the correct elementary-event indexing; the limiting derivative formula and the final theorems have not been disproved. The proposed correction is a mathematical repair identified here, not an author-adopted correction or an independently accepted revision.

LX=(d lambda-1)X-2 lambda H; LH(A)=2(d+1)lambda, LH(split)=2d lambda; D''(0)=4lambda^2>0. At d3 lambda1/6 v1 exact output D''=1/9. Recorded evidence: Counterevidence: Equation(20) retains correct edge indexing; corrected whole-state finite-increment kernel tends to it. report: Abstract: This review concerns the frozen 42-page arXiv version 2401.15904v3, dated 21 August 2024, by Morris Ang, Xin Sun, Pu Yu and Zijie Zhuang. Three demonstrated problems concern the uniqueness characterization of the nested-path exponent, a covariance normalization, and an inconsistent length-moment parameter in the main calculation. Each has a concrete local correction or a sharply specified correction requirement. The evidence does not disprove the existence of the exponent, the displayed closed forms, or the final conformal-radius moment theorems. This is an initial review, with scientific decision pending and no independent human acceptance recorded.
Author: AI-assisted technical review

Title: Initial technical review of
Boundary touching probability and nested-path exponent for non-simple CLE
# Source, scope and principal conclusions

The assigned identity is M25-0502, associated with journal DOI https://doi.org/10.1214/24-AOP1722. The scientific source actually examined is [paper], not an asserted equivalent of the journal version. All page locators below are the physical and printed pages of that 42-page PDF. Its SHA256 is

The text of all 42 pages, including references, was read in the current scientific conversation. The source pages carrying the findings and their counterevidence were additionally rendered and actually viewed. Exact file, computation and page-view bindings accompany this report.

The paper derives the probability that the CLE loop around the origin touches the boundary, refines conformal-radius moments according to that event, and uses those moments to determine a nested-path exponent. The internal proof route is the radial exploration description in Section 2, a welding identity in Theorem 3.1, the moment ratio in Proposition 4.4, Theorems 1.1–1.3, and the large-deviation argument of Section 5. The problems below occur on that route. Major severity here denotes a false main characterization or an invalid core mathematical step in the reviewed version; it does not assert that every conclusion is false.
# The exponent equation has an extraneous root

Equation reference: eq:raw. Problem 1 (Major: Theorem 1.4 does not uniquely characterize the exponent as printed).  Theorem 1.4, p. 4, equation (1.8), asserts uniqueness among \(x<1-\kappa/8\), for every \(a>0\) and \(4<\kappa<8\), of the solution to \[
 \sin u=a\sin(ru),\qquad
 u=\frac{\pi}{4}\sqrt{(\kappa-4)^2+8\kappa x},\qquad
 r=\frac{8-\kappa}{\kappa}.\] The definition of \(\operatorname{Root}(a)\) and the first paragraph of Section 5, p. 36, use this uniqueness.

Equation reference: eq:two-roots. Decisive counterexample. Put \(x_0=-(\kappa-4)^2/(8\kappa)\). Then \(u=0\), so both sides of [eq:raw] (#eq:raw) vanish for every \(a>0\). Moreover \(x_0<0<1-\kappa/8\), so the stated upper bound does not remove this root. At the admissible parameters \(\kappa=6\), \(a=1\), there are two distinct permitted roots: \[
 x_0=-\frac1{12},\qquad x_1=\frac5{48}<\frac14.\] The corresponding radicands are \(0\) and \(9\); at \(x_1\) the sine arguments are \(3\pi/4\) and \(\pi/4\). This proves nonuniqueness using exact algebra and elementary trigonometry.

There is also a direct probabilistic check on the spurious value. For \(a=1\), the expectation in (1.7) is a probability and hence at most one. An asymptotic \(\varepsilon^{-1/12+o(1)}\) would diverge as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Thus \(x_0\) cannot be its exponent at these parameters. ◻
## Counterevidence and correction

Equation reference: eq:moment, eq:sinc. Theorem 1.3, p. 3, gives a ratio of sines, rather than the cross-multiplied equation. With \(R=\operatorname{CR}(0,\widetilde D)\) on \(T^c\), its relevant moment is \[
 M_\kappa(x)=\mathbb E[R^{-x}\mathbf1_{T^c}]
 =\frac{\sin(ru)}{\sin u},\qquad x<1-\kappa/8.\] At \(x_0\) the removable value is \(M_\kappa(x_0)=r\). The intended characterization is \(aM_\kappa(x)=1\). Equivalently, using the entire extension \(\operatorname{sinc}z=\sin z/z\) with \(\operatorname{sinc}0=1\), it is \[
 \operatorname{sinc}u=ar\,\operatorname{sinc}(ru).\] This retains \(x_0\) exactly when \(a=\kappa/(8-\kappa)\); simply forbidding \(x_0\) for every \(a\) would introduce a different error. For negative radicand the ratios have their real hyperbolic-sine continuation.

Conditional on the paper’s moment identity, this correction has a unique solution. Indeed \(0<R<1\) on an event of positive probability, so \(M_\kappa\) is strictly increasing on its finite domain. It tends to zero at the left endpoint \(x\to-\infty\), by the hyperbolic-sine ratio, and to infinity as \(x\uparrow1-\kappa/8\), where \(u\uparrow\pi\) and \(\sin(r\pi)>0\). The moment is continuous on the intervening domain. This also justifies the inverse moment function used in Section 5.

Equation (1.9), p. 5, independently selects \(5/48\) at \(\kappa=6,a=1\). This is positive counterevidence against a failure of the intended exponent formula. A reader may infer that cancellation and a removable limit were intended, but the literal sine equation still has the extra zero. The theorem statement and the definition of \(\operatorname{Root}(a)\) need the corrected condition. This finding does not refute the subsequent large-deviation strategy.
# The stated Brownian covariance is impossible

Equation reference: eq:cov. Problem 2 (Major: the covariance in equation (3.7) is not positive semidefinite).  On p. 20, Section 3.3, the paper sets \[\mathbf a^2=\frac{2}{\sin(\pi\gamma^2/4)}\] and defines its two-dimensional Brownian motion by \[
 \operatorname{Var}(L_t)=\operatorname{Var}(R_t)=t,\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(L_t,R_t)
 =-\cos(\pi\gamma^2/4)\mathbf a^2t .\] Here \(\gamma=4/\sqrt\kappa\) and \(4<\kappa<8\). The excursion measures immediately following (3.7) are based on this motion.

Decisive covariance test. Take the interior value \(\kappa=6\), so \(\gamma^2=8/3\), \(\pi\gamma^2/4=2\pi/3\), and \(\mathbf a^2=4/\sqrt3\). For any \(t>0\), [eq:cov] (#eq:cov) gives \[\Sigma_t=t\begin{pmatrix}1&2/\sqrt3\\2/\sqrt3&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det\Sigma_t=-\frac{t^2}{3}<0.\] Equivalently \(\operatorname{Var}(L_t-R_t)=2t-4t/\sqrt3<0\). This contradicts a necessary covariance property of any real random vector, irrespective of Gaussianity. Neither an endpoint convention nor an unspecified drift can correct it. ◻
## Dependency, counterevidence and repair boundary

The excursion laws built from (3.7) enter the mating-of-trees description in Section 3.3 and the proof of the welding result in Section 3.4. Theorem 3.1 then feeds Proposition 4.3 and the conformal-radius calculation. The printed stochastic input is therefore invalid in a core construction.

Equation reference: eq:fixed-cov. The sentence preceding (3.7) calls \(\mathbf a^2\) a variance, strongly suggesting a missing diagonal factor. The coherent covariance \[
 \operatorname{Var}(L_t)=\operatorname{Var}(R_t)=\mathbf a^2t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(L_t,R_t)=-\mathbf a^2
       \cos(\pi\gamma^2/4)t\] has positive eigenvalues for \(\sqrt2<\gamma<2\) and determinant \(4t^2\). It preserves the stated correlation parameter. Alternatively one can use unit variances and remove \(\mathbf a^2\) from the off-diagonal term, with the associated change of time normalization.

These are mathematical normalization options, not a claim that all quantum-area and excursion-measure constants have thereby been audited. The paper should specify the intended time normalization and propagate it through its cited input. The local evidence is compatible with a typographical omission, and supplies no counterexample to Theorem 3.1 or to the final moment formulas.
# The length-moment parameter violates the invoked hypotheses

Equation reference: eq:bad-p. Problem 3 (Major: equations (4.15) and (4.21) use inconsistent exponents).  Lemma 4.9, p. 33, equation (4.15), takes \(Q<\alpha<4/\gamma\) and writes \[
 p=\frac{\gamma\alpha}{2}-1
 \ \in\ \left(\frac{\gamma^2}{4}-1,0\right).\] The same definition is repeated at the end of the proof of Proposition 4.4, p. 36. Lemma 4.7, pp. 32–33, requires \(\gamma^2/4-1<p<0\), and Lemma 4.5, pp. 30–31, requires \(-1<p<0\). They are used in Lemma 4.10 and in the proof of Proposition 4.4.

     =\frac{\gamma\alpha}{2}-2.\] Its image is exactly \((\gamma^2/4-1,0)\). At the concrete example \(p_*=-1/6\). The hypotheses of Lemma 2.22 hold here: \(\beta=\gamma<Q\) and \(\alpha+\gamma/2>Q\). ◻

Replacing the two explicit definitions by [eq:good-p] (#eq:good-p) also reconciles the last trigonometric simplification on p. 36 with Proposition 4.4.  B=\frac{2-g/2}{g}(g/2+2-2v).\] These are respectively \((\gamma-2/\gamma)(Q-\alpha)\) and \((2/\gamma-\gamma/2)(Q-\alpha)\). With \(p_*=v-2\), the two sine arguments divided by \(\pi\) in the last display on p. 36 satisfy the exact identities \[\begin{split}

 -g/4-4/g-4p_*/g+p_*&=B-2.
 \end{split}\] Thus their sine ratio is \(\sin(\pi A)/\sin(\pi B)\); also \(-\cos(\pi g/4)=\cos(\pi(1-g/4))\). The resulting expression is exactly (4.5), with the denominator \(2/\gamma-\gamma/2\) as actually printed on p. 29.

This supplies strong internal counterevidence to a false final formula. It is more than an unexplained interval typo: the power of the length difference in (4.21), the definition of the function in (4.15), and the admissibility of the integral evaluations must consistently use \(p_*\). The demonstrated issue is an invalid core derivation as written. The repair above restores these local steps; it does not independently reprove every external welding identity.
# Assumptions, boundary checks and review limits

The parameter checks along the reviewed dependency route are as follows. For \(4<\kappa<8\), one has \(2<\gamma^2<4\); the radial force parameter \(\rho=\kappa-6\) is greater than \(-2\). The stable-process index \(4/\gamma^2\) lies in \((1,2)\), and the inverse-time subordinator index \(\gamma^2/4\) lies in \((1/2,1)\). The triangle weights used in (4.17) are positive: \[W_1=3\gamma^2/2-2>\gamma^2/2,\quad
 0<W_2=2-\gamma^2/2<\gamma^2/2,\quad
 0<W_3=\gamma^2-2<\gamma^2/2.\] This agrees with the thick/thin distinctions of the stated decomposition. The interval \(Q<\alpha<4/\gamma\) is nonempty; the corrected \(p_*\) lies in \((-1,0)\). In the proof of Lemma 4.7, \(W'=-2p_*\) is positive and less than \(2-\gamma^2/2<\gamma^2/2\). The use of finite or sigma-finite surface measures is distinguished from probability normalization as specified at the start of Section 2.

Theorem 1.3’s removable value and its moment-domain endpoint were checked in Problem 1. The special value \(\kappa=6\) is an interior test, so the two explicit counterexamples do not depend on limiting CLE constructions at \(\kappa=4\) or \(8\). The formulas of Theorem 1.2 were independently evaluated at five interior \(\kappa\)-values and four nonnegative moment parameters; their two event contributions add to (1.2), within ordinary floating-point error. This is useful transcription and counterevidence checking, not a proof of the all-parameter probabilistic identities. Exact rational checks also verified the exponents and the repaired trigonometric identities above.

All substantive arguments here were carried out in the current scientific conversation. The saved Python calculation uses only the standard library and no author code. Its exact rational identities, negative determinant, and the analytic proofs in this report are the decisive evidence; the numerical tables are supplementary.

The paper’s external CLE exploration, imaginary-geometry, LCFT and welding results remain cited inputs, not independently reconstructed theories. No inference that a code supplement is necessary for these mathematical results is made. The arXiv history inspected for this review lists v3 as its latest revision; an author’s publication page links this preprint. Targeted correction searches did not identify an applicable erratum. Such searches do not prove that none exists. The journal version was not acquired and compared here; these findings are explicitly restricted to the frozen v3.
# Assessment

The reviewed version needs a moment-based uniqueness statement in Theorem 1.4, a consistent Brownian covariance normalization, and a consistent length exponent in the proof of Proposition 4.4. Each issue is established directly under admissible interior parameters or by an exact symbolic identity. The identified local repairs and the paper’s own consistent formulas should accompany any request for correction. A claim that the final theorems have been disproved would exceed the evidence. Scientific disposition remains pending independent review.
